P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Yes, freely. Uganda fully liberalised its capital account in 1997, and the Foreign Exchange Act 2004 repealed the Exchange Control Act. No surrender or repatriation rule for individuals' service income was found. The Governor may impose temporary exchange controls only after a severe balance-of-payments deterioration. Cross-border foreign-currency payments go through licensed institutions.

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Yes. Since 1997 residents may hold foreign-currency accounts in Ugandan banks. For example, Standard Chartered Uganda offers its current account in UGX, USD, GBP and EUR, and Ugandans open it with a national ID.

P4_paypal.question: Can residents receive money via PayPal?
P4_paypal.answer: UNCLEAR. Uganda is a listed PayPal market but not on the Payouts list, so platforms paying via PayPal Payouts cannot pay Ugandan accounts. A 2025 Ugandan guide describes withdrawing PayPal balances to a linked Ugandan Visa/Mastercard debit card. Other 2026 guides describe PayPal as having limited functionality in Uganda and recommend Payoneer.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: A sole trader working under their own true surname (with or without first names or initials) is not required to register a business name. Registration is required when trading under any other name (Business Names Registration Act). Business names are registered online with URSB (OBRS). In practice, gateways such as Pesapal (P3) and the citizens' 3-year income tax exemption (L7) require a registered business. A local trading licence may also apply but was not researched.

L1_registration.notes: The Act was renumbered Cap. 105 in the 2023 revised laws; the Cap. 109 text was read. The URSB fee schedule was not captured.

L2_tax_id.question: Tax ID: who needs one, how to get it?
L2_tax_id.answer: The TIN from the Uganda Revenue Authority (URA). Individuals with a National Identification Number (NIN) from NIRA can get an instant TIN online, without URA staff approval, in about 5 minutes. No documents are needed with a valid NIN, and details auto-populate from NIRA. Those without a NIN use the standard individual registration route.

sources.quote: No documents required if the applicant has a valid NIN/BRN

L2_tax_id.notes: Whether URA charges any fee is not stated on these pages (press reports say the service is free).

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Residents (permanent home in Uganda, or 183+ days in a 12-month period, among other tests) are taxed on income from all geographical sources. From 1 July 2026 (Income Tax (Amendment) Act 2026, signed 20 August 2026 with effect from 1 July), resident individuals pay nil up to UGX 4,020,000 a year, then 20%, 25%, and 30% above UGX 5,820,000, plus an additional 10% above UGX 120 million. Presumptive (turnover) tax applies to small businesses with sales of UGX 10m–150m, but professionals are excluded.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: VAT is 18%. Exports of goods and services are zero-rated (input VAT recoverable). The registration threshold rose from UGX 150m to UGX 300m a year (UGX 75m in any three consecutive months) from 1 July 2026, under the VAT (Amendment) Act 2026, assented 18 May 2026.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: The Data Protection and Privacy Act 2019. Every person, institution or public body that collects, processes, holds or uses personal data must register with the Personal Data Protection Office (PDPO, within NITA-U), under s.29 and reg. 15(1). Failing to register is an offence (fine and/or up to three months' imprisonment). No exemption notice for small operators was found.

L6_consumer_ecommerce.question: Consumer-protection / e-commerce rules for online sales (refunds, disclosures)
L6_consumer_ecommerce.answer: Electronic Transactions Act 2011. Online sellers must give prescribed information (s.24). If they fail to, the consumer may cancel within 14 days of receiving the goods or services (s.24(3)). Otherwise a consumer may cancel an electronic transaction within 7 days of receipt of the goods or services, or within 7 days of concluding the agreement (s.25).

L6_consumer_ecommerce.notes: Whether a newer consumer-protection statute applies to online sales was not checked. ULII returned 403 and the NITA FAQ URL 404.

L7_incentives.question: Legal incentives / tax holidays / special zones relevant to small digital businesses
L7_incentives.answer: (1) A three-year income tax exemption for businesses established by citizens after 1 July 2025 (Income Tax (Amendment) Act 2025). Conditions: registered investment capital up to UGX 500m, no prior use by the citizen or an associate, and annual returns plus a business information return. The ITA definition of 'citizen' covers EAC partner-state citizens. (2) The VAT threshold doubled to UGX 300m (L4). (3) Exports are zero-rated (L4). (4) No foreign-exchange controls (P1).

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; platforms that pay out through PayPal Payouts cannot pay PayPal accounts here (not on PayPal's Payouts list, see P4 for ordinary PayPal receiving); Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
